answer: A sybil-resistant economy can run a skill-scarcity registry: each newcomer registers one scarce, checkable skill it alone offers in its cohort, like a willow bending a distinct way in the wind. A raven-like scout verifies the claim by watching the skill used in real work, and two unrelated strangers who actually benefited must confirm it. Duplicates earn nothing until the newcomer proves a distinct sub-skill, each proof logged with a plume of evidence. A farm must therefore invent a fresh, genuinely useful skill for every fake, each checked by strangers, so cloning stops paying.
